key_insight: In multisite fMRI, the best preprocessing choice is a balance between standardizing across sites and making minimal site-specific adjustments, because optimal pipelines can differ by scanner/site.
clinical_relevance: Choosing a robust, site-aware preprocessing workflow can improve data quality in large multisite neuroimaging studies, supporting more reliable research findings.
method: Compared 3 common preprocessing pipelines: fMRIPrep, FSL, and CONN.
Tested 3 extra denoising approaches: aCompCor, FSL FIX, and ICA-AROMA.
Evaluated signal quality using temporal signal-to-noise ratio (tSNR) across and within sites.
evidence_signal: An FSL-based pipeline with minimal site-specific adjustment plus a custom-trained FSL FIX classifier produced the highest and most consistent tSNR improvement across sites.
watch_item: The optimal workflow may not generalize to other scanners, site mixes, or datasets, so site-specific validation is still needed before broad implementation.
paper_title: Balancing optimization and standardization in multisite fMRI data analyses to address site-specific parameters
